explanation: Copying values into an auxiliary sequence gives direct access to mirrored positions without modifying singly linked links. Comparing only the first half tests each required mirrored pair once.
correctness: The auxiliary sequence is exactly the original head-to-tail value sequence because each node is read once in order. A sequence is a palindrome exactly when positions i and n-1-i are equal for every i below n/2. Rejecting the first unequal pair or accepting after all these comparisons implements that condition. The traversal never writes any node field, so every exit preserves the input.
walkthrough: For [3,8,1,8,3], copy the five values. Compare positions 0 and 4 (3=3), then positions 1 and 3 (8=8); the middle 1 needs no partner. Return true. Replacing the final value by 4 makes the first comparison fail, without changing a link.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for traversal and mirrored comparisons.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the copied values.
edgeCases: Empty, one-node, even-length, and odd-length lists.
Repeated values alone do not guarantee a palindrome.
Early rejection must preserve all original links.
